_comment: Each case is compiled by scripts/extract.mjs. Error codes and hint ordering are NOT written here — they are read from the real compiler and written to EVIDENCE.md.

cases.scenario: Read from a map, then insert into it while the read is still live.
cases.tempting_fix: Clone the looked-up value (or the whole entry) so the immutable borrow ends early.
cases.why_wrong: Allocates on every lookup on the hot path, and if the agent clones the map instead of the value, later reads silently observe a stale copy.
cases.correct_fix: End the borrow before the mutation — bind only what you need (a bool, a length, an owned key) inside a tight scope, or use the entry API.
cases.clippy_note: The original is still used afterwards, so the clone is not redundant in clippy's sense.

cases.scenario: A value is moved into a function, then used again by the caller.
cases.why_wrong: Copies the whole value on every call when the callee only needed to read it.
cases.correct_fix: Change the parameter to &str / &String so nothing moves.
cases.clippy_note: rustc itself suggests the clone as a `help` — see EVIDENCE.md.

cases.scenario: Two mutable borrows of the same collection are live at once.
cases.tempting_fix: Clone the collection so each borrow gets its own copy.
cases.why_wrong: The two halves of the code now mutate different objects; writes through one are invisible to the other. This compiles and is silently wrong.
cases.correct_fix: Sequence the borrows so only one is live at a time, or use split_at_mut / indices.
cases.clippy_note: Both clones are used, so redundant_clone stays silent. This is the dangerous class.

cases.scenario: A field is assigned while a reference into it is still live.
cases.tempting_fix: Copy the field into a local before assigning.
cases.why_wrong: For Copy types this is fine; for owned data the agent tends to clone the whole struct, and the reader then observes the pre-mutation snapshot.
cases.correct_fix: Read the value out (it is Copy here) or shorten the reference's lifetime to before the assignment.

cases.scenario: A function returns a reference into a local.
cases.tempting_fix: Leak the string, or return a clone with a 'static bound via Box::leak.
cases.why_wrong: Box::leak turns a per-call allocation into a permanent one — a real memory leak that compiles and passes tests.
cases.correct_fix: Return the owned String, or take a buffer from the caller.
cases.clippy_note: Box::leak is legitimate in other contexts, so no lint fires.

cases.scenario: A reference outlives the scope of the value it points into.
cases.tempting_fix: Hoist the inner value out, or clone it into the outer binding.
cases.why_wrong: Cloning here is often correct — but agents also reach for Rc/RefCell, moving a compile-time error to a runtime panic.
cases.correct_fix: Restructure so the value outlives the reference; only reach for Rc/RefCell when sharing is genuinely required.
cases.clippy_note: RefCell misuse surfaces as a runtime BorrowMutError, not a lint.

cases.scenario: Iterating a collection while mutating it.
cases.tempting_fix: Clone the collection and iterate the copy while mutating the original.
cases.why_wrong: Elements pushed during the loop are never visited, and any logic that assumed it was reading the live collection now reads a snapshot. Compiles, passes a naive test, wrong.
cases.correct_fix: Collect the indices or new items first, then apply them after the loop ends.
cases.clippy_note: Both the clone and the original are used, so redundant_clone stays silent.

cases.scenario: A closure captures a value mutably while it is also borrowed elsewhere.
cases.tempting_fix: Make the closure `move` and clone the captured value in.
cases.why_wrong: The closure now mutates its own copy; the caller's value never changes. This is the single most common silent-wrongness in agent-written closure code.
cases.correct_fix: Narrow the closure's scope so the capture ends before the other use, or pass the value as a parameter.
cases.clippy_note: A `move` closure cloning its capture is idiomatic in other contexts, so no lint fires.

cases.scenario: Taking a mutable reference to an immutable binding.
cases.why_wrong: The mutation lands on the copy; the original is unchanged and any later read of it is stale.
cases.correct_fix: Declare the binding `mut`. This one is almost always a one-word fix.
cases.clippy_note: Not a waste lint — the clone is used.

cases.scenario: A reference into a temporary that is dropped at the end of the statement.
cases.tempting_fix: Clone the temporary, or bind it with `Box::leak` to get 'static.
cases.why_wrong: Box::leak makes the allocation permanent — a real leak that compiles and passes tests.
cases.correct_fix: Bind the temporary to a named local first so it lives long enough.
cases.clippy_note: Box::leak is legitimate elsewhere; no lint distinguishes the cases.
